title: Ciro's in Hollywood and the help not socializing
summary: The band was first to play Ciro's and Duke is told not to sit with guests.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, when you were playing out in California you -- there -- you didn't have to be -- you weren't bothered with the segregated policies were you.

Oh, no, California was heaven. They never lowered the boom on us with that jive. No, because we were celebrities. They never tell us what to do and what not to do. We go where we want to go. We played Ciro's in Hollywood, the biggest cafe, Ciro's in Hollywood. So I recall on opening night at Ciro's. You heard of the famous Ciro's? That was the cabaret. They never had no colored band, we were the first one. We played out there on a month's engagement, so I recall opening night, that's where all the Hollywood stars hung out.

So we was playing and the stage door let out from the stage in the alley. Got to come there, come to the stage door, to come to the stage so the first night, man, we ain't never run in no segregation, so the first night different people from New York -- New York actors and big stars, so they come over and so Duke went down and sit at the table with them because he's a star, so this cat, this Greek or whoever he was, he say listen Mr. Ellington, we don't allow the help to socialize with the guests, I say, 'Duke don't say nothing.'
